articles.title: Sesame Street Transforms Chappell Roan’s ‘Hot to Go!’ Into the Potty-Training Anthem ‘Got to Go,’ With Lead Vocals From Cookie Monster
articles.summary: Sesame Street has a half-century-long tradition of legendary musical guests and innovative adaptations: from Stevie Wonder’s iconic performance in the early ‘70s to Tony Bennett retrofitting his timeless classic “Fly Me to the Moon” to be a story about the show’s worm character Slimy on an…
body: It’s a note-for-note rendition too, complete with the song’s chanted middle section from guest vocalists Elmo and Abby Cadabby. And although we don’t get to see Muppets doing the world-famous hand-gestures spelling out the song’s title, instead we get singing letters spelling out POTTY.

Contacted by Variety, a rep for Chappell Roan said the singer had no comment. Indeed, none was necessary: Granting permission for her and cowriter/producer Dan Nigro’s song to be used in such an amusing and imaginatively instructive way — for young children, no less — is a statement in itself.

articles.title: ‘Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie’ Review: Alex Gibney Profiles the Controversial Author During His Harrowing Hospitalization
articles.summary: There’s nothing more distressing in “Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie’ than the unflinching closeups of the author’s wounded body in the days and weeks after August 12, 2022, when he was repeatedly stabbed while on stage at a literary festival in upstate New York.
body: Rushdie, with the help of his wife Rachel Eliza Griffiths, bares his scars in the days and weeks after being violently attacked, in this standard but comprehensive portrait of the writer’s life under fire.

But lest we dismiss these events as contained to the past, the 2022 assault stands as a reminder that artistic expression remains as frighteningly vulnerable as Rushdie’s brutalized body. That message might feel obvious for anyone even remotely tapped into the American news cycle, but it’s given a weighty (if obligatorily sentimental) personal touch by the resilient Rushdie and his support system, led by the tenacious Griffiths — his rock against a seemingly neverending saga.

articles.title: ‘Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom’ Was Inspired by Universal Monsters and Hammer Horror Movies
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This story contains major spoilers for “Shaun The Sheep: The Beast Of Mossy Bottom,” now in theaters. Shaun the Sheep is back for his third feature-length film, “Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom.” This time around, Shaun and his fellow sheep are getting ready for Halloween…
body: Speaking with Variety, the film’s directors Steve Cox and Matthew Walker, explained that the initial idea was for it to be a Valentine’s Day special. “It was always the idea of the farmer having a relationship with someone, but then at some point, the idea of a monster came up,” says Walker. “And the ideas got combined at some point. Then the natural progression of that was it being a Halloween special.”

As the ideas evolved, the story of Shaun being a mad scientist emerged as an early concept the team loved. Aardman’s stop-motion studio is no stranger to doing monster movies, having previously produced “Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit.” If they were going to tackle another monster movie, they wanted it to look completely different.

articles.title: ‘The man’s a psychopath when it comes to hedgerows’: Derek vs Derek, the unexpectedly heartwarming doc about farmers at war
articles.summary: One Devon farmer, called Derek, is committed to rewilding his land. His neighbour, also a Derek, tends cattle and crops. What happened when a film-maker decided to follow the bickering pair? Derek Gow and Derek Banbury should hate each other.
body: “It’s like he’s just gone mad,” says Banbury of Gow at the start of Derek vs Derek, an illuminating and unexpectedly funny new documentary that follows the pair over three years. “And the madness is now crossing the road on to my land.”

What begins as a portrait of neighbours at war, with no hope of bridging the chasm between modern chemical farmers and idealistic rewilders, or between the needs of food production and the worsening extinction crisis, is slowly and subtly upended, as the two Dereks learn to live alongside each other and hopeful seeds of common ground are sown.

Documentary-maker James Dawson started following Gow as he sold the last of his sheep, planning a film about the dramatic changes brought about by rewilding his farm. Then, when Dawson first visited Gow, he was put up at the Banburys, where wife Linda has turned former pigsties and old sheds into holiday cottages. As soon as Dawson met Derek Banbury over breakfast in the farmhouse kitchen, he knew he had to make a rather different film.

articles.title: Zack Snyder is angling to make another Batman movie. Stranger things have happened
articles.summary: Two Batman projects are already in the making at DC Studios, but Snyder has set his sights on the classic Frank Miller graphic novel The Dark Knight Returns. There cannot be too many film-makers who have spent quite so long being told that their version of a superhero universe is over, as Zack…
body: In an interview with Variety to promote his forthcoming film The Last Photograph, Snyder returned to an idea he has been talking about for years: adapting Miller’s famously grim 1986 vision of an ageing Batman coming out of retirement in a dystopian Gotham. “The reason why it’s The Dark Knight Returns, if anyone would ever let me do it outside of the DC Universe since it’s a novel that just happens to have superheroes in it, is if I could do Watchmen and The Dark Knight Returns, those two books next to each other, to me, represent the complete cycle of the superhero comic book medium,” the film-maker said.

“You can do no more than those two books. Watchmen came at the beginning of the superhero movie phase, so it would be super fitting to have The Dark Knight Returns come now, at what I would say is possibly – I don’t want to call it the twilight, but – we’re down the road of the superhero movie genre, and I think audiences would understand the why of it.”

articles.title: Werner Herzog Picks Up San Sebastian’s Donostia Award at Politically Charged Opening Ceremony
articles.summary: The evening's hosts, Fariba Sheikhan and Mariona Terés, kicked off the proceedings by condemning the Israel-Gaza war and declaring support for 'NAZA' directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor.
body: German director, screenwriter and producer Werner Herzog touched on the Pyrenees and poetry as he picked up San Sebastian Film Festival ‘s most prestigious honor Friday night in what was a politically charged opening ceremony.
Herzog was recognized with the coveted Donostia Award at the Kursaal Theatre in northern Spain, with a raucous standing ovation from his fellow European creatives.

“I’m here standing in front of you, not as a foreigner,” he continued. “I’ve had a connection to you, the Basque people, through an early film of mine — [1972’s] Aguirre, the Wrath of God,” said Herzog, explaining that he traveled — on foot — “many, many years ago” from the Cannes Film Festival up into the Pyrenees mountain range. It was more than 1,000 kilometers, said the director. “But I must confess, I ended up in Biarritz,” he laughed, “not San Sebastian.”

articles.title: Iranian actor Laleh Marzban faces severe threats after Venice film festival speech
articles.summary: Marzban, who won a best actress award for her portrayal of a woman held hostage by her father in Falling House, has received condemnations from authorities after dedicating her prize to ‘the women of Iran’ An Iranian actress who won the best newcomer award at the Venice film festival has come under…
body: Laleh Marzban last Saturday won the best actress award in the Orizzonti sidebar competition for emerging talent, for her role in Mohsen Gharaei’s Falling House, a film revolving around three generations of women who are incarcerated in their own home by the family’s father.

At the awards gala, Marzban dedicated her prize to “the women of my country who have paid the highest price for even the smallest measure of freedom”. Speaking in Farsi, she added that Iranians were experiencing some of the most difficult days of their lives but should not lose hope.

On Thursday, the Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution, a conservative-dominated government body appointed by Iran’s supreme leader, issued a statement condemning Marzban’s speech as “presenting a one-sided narrative of Iran’s proud society”.

Referring only to “recent statements and behaviour made at the Venice film festival”, it said reducing Iranian women to “the stereotypes desired by western circles is not in line with the awareness-raising mission and social commitment of art”.

articles.title: Pulp: What Do You Do for an Encore? review – Jarvis Cocker’s wit and warmth upstage the hits
articles.summary: Wonderful archive footage charts the Sheffield outsiders’ unlikely rise, but the distant camerawork struggles to capture the thrill of their triumphant O2 gigs. In 1978, in the classroom of a comprehensive school in Sheffield, a skinny, shortsighted 15-year-old wrote a mission statement in the back…
body: In 2023, after a hiatus of a decade, his band Pulp started touring again, and last year played to 20,000 people at each of two nights at the O2 in London. This film features concert footage from those gigs in which a still lithe, still-got-it-at-60-odd Jarvis Cocker sings his hit art-pop anthems backed by most of the classic lineup and a 10-piece string section. And interspersed with the concert footage are autobiographical musings, nostalgic archive footage, interviews with Jarvis’s mum and gran, and Cocker narrating the story of how he got from there, almost half a century ago, to here.

The total package, in typical Pulp style, is a mixture of the exuberant and celebratory with the bittersweet and reflective. In voiceover, Cocker says that songs “contain pockets of energy from your past life that’s released again when you perform them”. And hearing them performed in the present, you notice how many of the lyrics were about young people wondering what life would be like when they were older. (“Let’s all meet up in the year 2000/Won’t it be strange when we’re all fully grown?”) Which was another way of them wondering whether they were making the right decisions in the present.

articles.title: The Rules These Horror Power Producers Swear by
articles.summary: Spooky Pictures' Roy Lee and Steven Schneider, and frequent partner Ben Ross of Image Nation look at the deals — and the philosophy — that helps them land project after project.
body: If you’re a producer in the competitive horror landscape, a piece of advice: get an early look at every hot script you can.

That’s one of the trade secrets of Spooky Pictures partners Roy Lee and Steven Schneider, who leverage their relationships to get scripts like Damien McCarthy’s Hokum “a minute early,” as Schneider says.

Released by Neon, Hokum film ended up grossing $25 million on a $5 million budget, and is one of three movies Spooky and Image Nation teamed up to release this year, including two fall festival entries: Casey Affleck’s The Company at Venice and Guy Nattiv’s The Liberation at Telluride and the Toronto International Film Festival, which wraps up this week.
Lee, Schneider and Ross don’t land every script they want, but the percentage is high.

articles.title: Tenko and Coronation Street actress Stephanie Cole dies aged 84
articles.summary: She was best known for playing Dr Beatrice Mason in the 1980s BBC wartime TV drama Tenko.
body: Actress Stephanie Cole, known for roles in Tenko, Open All Hours and Coronation Street, has died aged 84.
A statement from her agent John Grant, issued on behalf of her family, confirmed the actress had been living with Alzheimer's for several years.
"Stephanie was an extraordinary talent whose long and distinguished career included many iconic performances in theatre and television," the statement read.
"She brought joy to millions through her many much-loved roles in sitcom and drama. She will also be remembered for her tireless work supporting mental health charities."
